correctness.rationale: Complete Catalan first-return enumeration gives \(2C_{j-1}\) excursions of semilength \(j\); Lagrange inversion gives \(a_{n,k}=[z^n]F(z)^k\). The marked-return decomposition proves the conditional law on its entire support. The adjacent conditional likelihood ratio reduces to \((u-q)/(2u-q-1)\), whose derivative in \(u\) is \((q-1)/(2u-q-1)^2\); the omitted rightmost support point ensures strict stochastic ordering even at q=1 and singleton-support boundaries. At \(q=1\) the ratio is constant on common support, so the conditional law is an exact truncation and its TV distance equals the removed mass. A standalone exact checker passes 438,359 assertions, including exhaustive bridges through 20 steps and formula/normalization/order checks through semilength 40. The proof, not computation, covers all n.

value.rationale: The chronological r-th return is an intrinsic mark of the local-time/renewal profile of a finite tied-down walk. The theorem establishes a full likelihood-ratio order, stronger than moment or stochastic comparisons, uniformly over every rank \(r\), bridge size \(n\) and return-count level \(k\). It implies ordering of all increasing return-time losses and yields a sharp exact conditioning/total-variation identity for the penultimate-return boundary. This is a natural structural dependence result with a complete domain, not an arbitrary fixed numerical instance.
